title: Evaluate network protocols, routing, and infrastructure design: concept decisions 3
teachingQuestion: For this flow, who receives it, which path/plane carries it, where does protection terminate, and what shared dependency can fail?
focalInsight: Addressing, delivery type, topology, plane separation, and cryptographic endpoints jointly determine actual reachability and failure exposure.
caption: Read across a row to connect meaning, decision and consequence. Use the retrieval answer to check your explanation after reading the linked scenario.

nodes.label: channel termination boundary
nodes.definition: Point where a cryptographic tunnel/session ends and protected traffic becomes subject to the next path/control set.
nodes.detail: Point where a cryptographic tunnel/session ends and protected traffic becomes subject to the next path/control set.
nodes.decision: Document termination, onward protection, authorization, inspection, logging, and failure behavior for each protected channel.
nodes.failureExample: TLS ends at a gateway and plaintext traffic traverses an untrusted internal segment.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Protection ends at the terminator; model the onward path separately.

nodes.label: anycast
nodes.definition: One address announced from multiple nodes so routing selects a reachable instance.
nodes.detail: One address announced from multiple nodes so routing selects a reachable instance.
nodes.decision: Use where locality/resilience helps, while monitoring which instance receives traffic and controlling consistent policy.
nodes.failureExample: Treating anycast as one fixed server leaves logs and policy incomplete.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Anycast is one address, multiple possible receivers.

nodes.label: Converged Protocols
nodes.definition: Protocols that carry storage, voice, compute, or similar services across shared network infrastructure.
nodes.detail: Protocols that carry storage, voice, compute, or similar services across shared network infrastructure.
nodes.decision: Assess shared capacity, trust, management, and common-mode failure effects before convergence.
nodes.failureExample: Voice and storage both fail when a shared fabric policy or controller is compromised.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Converged services share dependencies; isolate and test the common failure paths.

nodes.label: Performance Metrics
nodes.definition: Bandwidth, throughput, latency, jitter, and signal-to-noise measures used to judge network service behavior.
nodes.detail: Bandwidth, throughput, latency, jitter, and signal-to-noise measures used to judge network service behavior.
nodes.decision: Assess against application/service requirements and security-control overhead or failure effects.
nodes.failureExample: Encryption inspection adds latency that breaks a real-time voice service.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Choose the metric that matches the service failure: jitter for voice timing, throughput for delivered volume.

nodes.label: Segmentation
nodes.definition: Network boundary policy that limits which paths/routes can connect different trust purposes.
nodes.detail: Network boundary policy that limits which paths/routes can connect different trust purposes.
nodes.decision: Enforce at routed/virtual boundaries and verify allowed/denied flows, management access, and exceptions.
nodes.failureExample: A route advertisement bypasses the intended segmentation firewall.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Segmentation requires route and enforcement verification, not only a subnet plan.

nodes.label: Authorization
nodes.definition: Permission decision for a principal or device to use a network service, management operation, or protected path.
nodes.detail: Permission decision for a principal or device to use a network service, management operation, or protected path.
nodes.decision: Check authority at the relevant endpoint/control point after identity is established and scope access narrowly.
nodes.failureExample: A valid VPN login is permitted to administer routers without a separate privilege check.
nodes.retrievalAnswer: Identity proves who; authorization decides which network action is permitted.
